title: CDN cache lifetime configuration
sidebarTitle: Configure CDN caching
ai-navigation: Configure CDN cache lifetime in the Customer Portal or via REST API with origin headers, a CDN lifetime, or per-code rules.
---

import { MethodSwitch, MethodSection } from "/snippets/method-switch.jsx";

<MethodSwitch>
  <MethodSection id="portal" label="Customer Portal">

<p>Choose where the cache lifetime comes from. Origin controlled uses caching headers from the origin and a fallback lifetime from the CDN settings. CDN controlled uses the lifetime configured on the CDN. In CDN controlled mode, an advanced rule overrides that lifetime for one response code.</p>

<Note>
Files users have not requested within 36 hours will be removed from the CDN servers' cache, regardless of the feature settings.
</Note>

## CDN caching configuration

<Info>
CDN caching eligibility is based on HTTP response status codes and `Cache-Control` headers, not on file extensions. All file types—including `.webp`, `.swf`, and others—follow the same caching rules as any other object.
</Info>

### Origin controlled

<p>If the origin does not already send `Cache-Control`, configure it before selecting Origin controlled. Then set the fallback cache expiry.</p>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Configure Cache-Control on the origin server">
    Skip this step when the origin already sends `Cache-Control`. Depending on the web server (Apache or Nginx), add the `Cache-Control` header with the `max-age` and `public` parameters to the `.htaccess` (for Apache) or `nginx.conf` (for Nginx) file.

    In `Cache-Control`, `public` permits shared-cache (CDN) storage, and `max-age` sets the freshness duration in seconds.

    The following Apache configuration caches `.gif` and `.ico` files for 4 days (`max-age=345600` seconds):

    ```apache
    <ifModule mod_headers.c>   
      <FilesMatch "\.(gif|ico)$">   
        Header set Cache-Control "max-age=345600, public"   
      </FilesMatch>   
    </ifModule>
    ```

    The following Nginx configuration caches `.ico`, `.css`, `.js`, `.gif`, `.jpeg`, and `.png` files for 1 day (86,400 seconds):

    ```nginx
    server {   
     #...   
      location ~* \.(?:ico|css|js|gif|jpeg|png)$ {   
        add_header Cache-Control "max-age=86400, public";   
      }   
     #...   
    }
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open the CDN resource settings">
    In the [Gcore&nbsp;Customer&nbsp;Portal](https://portal.gcore.com), navigate to **CDN** > **CDN resources** and click the CNAME of the resource where the `Cache-Control` header is configured.

    <Frame>![CDN resources list page](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/cdn-resources.png)</Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Navigate to CDN caching">
    Navigate to **Cache** > **CDN caching**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Confirm Origin controlled is selected">
    Confirm that **Origin controlled** is selected in the dropdown.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Set the default cache expiry">
    Specify the timespan in the **Default cache expiry** field. Select a predefined value from the list or select **Custom value** and enter the time in seconds. This value is used as a fallback when the origin does not send caching HTTP headers.

    <Info>
    For Origin controlled mode, CDN servers store responses with codes `200`, `201`, `204`, `206`, `301`, `302`, `303`, `307`, and `308`. A `304 Not Modified` response is not independently stored; it revalidates and extends an existing cached entry. Responses with other codes are not cached.
    </Info>

    <Frame>![CDN caching settings with Origin controlled selected](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/cdn-caching-origin-controlled.png)</Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save changes">
    Click **Save changes**.
  </Step>
</Steps>

### CDN controlled

<p>CDN caching can be configured at two levels:</p>

  * For the whole resource

  * At the advanced caching rule level in the resource

<p>These settings are independent — CDN caching can be set to **Do not cache** in the main settings while enabled in an advanced rule, and vice versa.</p>

<Warning>
CDN caching applies only to responses with status codes `200`, `206`, `301`, and `302`. Responses with `4xx` and `5xx` status codes are not cached by default. To cache `404` or other non-default status codes, configure an advanced caching rule under the **Enable CDN caching via advanced caching rules** tab below.
</Warning>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Enable CDN caching for the whole resource">
    <Steps>
      <Step title="Open CDN resources">
        In the Customer Portal, navigate to **CDN** > **CDN resources**.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Open the resource settings">
        Click the CNAME of the required resource to open its settings.

        <Frame>![CDN resources list page](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/cdn-resources.png)</Frame>
      </Step>
      <Step title="Navigate to CDN caching">
        Navigate to **Cache** > **CDN caching**.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Enable CDN caching">
        Confirm the **Enable CDN caching** toggle is enabled. If not, click the toggle to enable it.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Select CDN controlled">
        Select **CDN controlled** from the dropdown.

        <Frame>![CDN caching settings with CDN controlled selected](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/cdn-caching-cdn-controlled.png)</Frame>
      </Step>
      <Step title="Set the cache expiry">
        Specify the caching timespan in the **Cache expiry** field. Select a predefined value from the list or select **Custom value** and enter a time in seconds.

        <Warning>
        If the **Do not cache** option is selected, caching is disabled even when the **Enable CDN caching** toggle is enabled.
        </Warning>
      </Step>
      <Step title="Configure advanced rules (optional)">
        Optionally, configure advanced caching rules for different caching times by response code.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Save changes">
        Click **Save changes**.
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Enable CDN caching via advanced caching rules">
    <Steps>
      <Step title="Navigate to CDN caching">
        In the CDN resource settings, navigate to **Cache** > **CDN caching**.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Enable CDN caching">
        Confirm the **Enable CDN caching** toggle is enabled. If not, click the toggle to enable it.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Select CDN controlled">
        Select **CDN controlled** from the dropdown.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Add a caching rule">
        Click **Add rule** and configure it as follows:

          * **Response code**: enter the HTTP response code to apply caching to.

          * **Caching time**: specify how long the data will be stored in the cache before it expires.

        <Frame>![Advanced caching rule form with Response code and Caching time fields](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/advanced-caching-rule.png)</Frame>

        The Caching time in advanced rules takes priority over the general Cache expiry.

        With a Cache expiry of 4 days and two advanced rules — one for the `200` response code configured for 10 minutes and another for `404` configured for 1 minute — requests are cached as follows:

          * Requests with response code `200`: cached for 10 minutes.
          * Requests with response code `404`: cached for 1 minute.
          * Requests with response codes `206`, `301`, and `302`: cached for 4 days.
          * Requests with response codes `4xx` (except `404`) and `5xx`: not cached.
      </Step>
      <Step title="Save changes">
        Click **Save changes** to apply the settings.
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Note>
For VOD and live streaming, use the video-specific cache lifetimes described in [caching rules](/cdn/getting-started/create-a-cdn-resource/create-a-cdn-resource-for-video-streaming#step-4-configure-caching-rules).
</Note>

## What happens when the cache lifetime expires

<p>When a cached file's lifetime expires, Gcore CDN performs conditional revalidation with the origin if the cached response includes a validator such as an [ETag](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/ETag) or `Last-Modified` header. The CDN sends a conditional request (`If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since`); if the origin responds with `304 Not Modified`, the cached copy is reused and its lifetime is reset. If the origin returns a new response, the CDN stores and serves the updated content.</p>

<p>If the cached response includes no validator, the CDN cannot perform conditional revalidation and must retrieve the full response from the origin after expiration.</p>

## CDN caching verification

<p>Request the file twice. A cacheable response returns `cache: MISS` when the CDN fetches it from the origin, then `cache: HIT` when the CDN serves it from cache.</p>

```sh
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://cdn.example.com/css/style.css
```

<p>Cache miss, fetched from the origin:</p>

```http
HTTP/2 200
cache: MISS
```

<p>Cache hit, served from the CDN cache:</p>

```http
HTTP/2 200
cache: HIT
x-cached-since: 2026-09-22T08:00:00+00:00
```

<p>In browser DevTools, open **Network**, reload the page, select a CDN-delivered file, and inspect its response headers.</p>

<Frame>![Browser DevTools Network tab showing response headers](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/specify-cache-lifetime-on-a-cdn-resource-or-origin/devtools-headers.png)</Frame>

### Caching response headers

| HTTP header | Explanation |
| --- | --- |
| CACHE: HIT | The file was served from the CDN cache. |
| CACHE: MISS | The file was not in the CDN cache and was fetched from the origin. If the response is cacheable under the current configuration, it is stored in cache and a later request can return CACHE: HIT. |
| CACHE: BYPASS | The CDN did not store the response. This happens when `Cache-Control` is `no-store` or `no-cache`. |
| X-Cached-Since | The UTC time when the file was stored on the CDN server. |
| X-ID | Identifier of the edge server that delivered the file. See [cache diagnostics](/cdn/troubleshooting/cache-percentage-is-low-how-to-solve-the-issue). |

<p>For content caching issues, check the origin settings or contact [Gcore&nbsp;Support](https://support.gcore.com/hc/en-us/requests/new).</p>

</MethodSection>
  <MethodSection id="api" label="REST API">

<p>Set how long CDN servers store an origin response. `default` follows origin cache headers and supplies a fallback lifetime. `value` sets one lifetime on the CDN. Files with no requests for 36 hours leave the cache regardless of this setting.</p>

<Info>
An [API&nbsp;token](/account-settings/api-tokens) is required. The CDN resource ID is visible under **CDN** → **CDN Resources**, or from the [resources&nbsp;list](/api-reference/cdn/cdn-resources/list-cdn-resources) call.
</Info>

<p>A [resource update](/api-reference/cdn/cdn-resources/change-cdn-resource) sets `options.edge_cache_settings`. Use `default` to follow origin cache headers with a fallback lifetime, or `value` to set the lifetime on the CDN. The two fields cannot be sent together, and one of them is required.</p>

<p>Open a terminal and export the required variables:</p>

```bash
export GCORE_API_KEY="{YOUR_API_KEY}"
export CDN_RESOURCE_ID="{YOUR_CDN_RESOURCE_ID}"
```

## Use origin cache headers

<p>Set `default` to the fallback lifetime used when the origin sends no caching headers. The fallback applies to responses `200`, `201`, `204`, `206`, `301`, `302`, `303`, `304`, `307`, and `308`. Other codes are not cached. A duration uses nginx time, such as `4d`, `12h`, or `10m`.</p>

<Info>
Send the full `edge_cache_settings` object on every update. Fields omitted from the object are removed.
</Info>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os

    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()
    resource_id = int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"])

    updated = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        resource_id,
        options={"edge_cache_settings": {"enabled": True, "default": "4d"}},
    )
    cache = updated.options.edge_cache_settings
    print(cache.enabled, cache.default)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "strconv"

        gcore "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go"
        "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go/cdn"
    )

    func main() {
        client := gcore.NewClient()
        ctx := context.Background()
        resourceID, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("CDN_RESOURCE_ID"), 10, 64)
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }

        updated, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                EdgeCacheSettings: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsEdgeCacheSettings{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Default: gcore.String("4d"),
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
        cache := updated.Options.EdgeCacheSettings
        fmt.Println(cache.Enabled, cache.Default)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="curl">
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH "https://api.gcore.com/cdn/resources/$CDN_RESOURCE_ID" \
      -H "Authorization: APIKey $GCORE_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "edge_cache_settings": {
            "enabled": true,
            "default": "4d"
          }
        }
      }'
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200. The saved option is:</p>

    ```json
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "default": "4d"
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Set a CDN cache lifetime

<p>Set `value` to ignore origin cache headers and store responses `200`, `206`, `301`, and `302` for that lifetime. Responses `4xx` and `5xx` are not cached unless `custom_values` names them. Sending `value` removes a previously saved `default`.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os

    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()
    resource_id = int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"])

    updated = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        resource_id,
        options={"edge_cache_settings": {"enabled": True, "value": "12h"}},
    )
    cache = updated.options.edge_cache_settings
    print(cache.enabled, cache.value)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "strconv"

        gcore "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go"
        "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go/cdn"
    )

    func main() {
        client := gcore.NewClient()
        ctx := context.Background()
        resourceID, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("CDN_RESOURCE_ID"), 10, 64)
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }

        updated, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                EdgeCacheSettings: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsEdgeCacheSettings{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Value:   gcore.String("12h"),
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
        cache := updated.Options.EdgeCacheSettings
        fmt.Println(cache.Enabled, cache.Value)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="curl">
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH "https://api.gcore.com/cdn/resources/$CDN_RESOURCE_ID" \
      -H "Authorization: APIKey $GCORE_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "edge_cache_settings": {
            "enabled": true,
            "value": "12h"
          }
        }
      }'
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200. The saved option is:</p>

    ```json
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "value": "12h"
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Set a lifetime for one response code

<p>Add `custom_values` next to `value` or `default`. Each key is a status code, or `any` for every code. These entries take priority over `value`. `10m` on `200` and `1m` on `404` override a `4d` lifetime for those codes only. Codes absent from the map keep `value`.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os

    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()
    resource_id = int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"])

    updated = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        resource_id,
        options={
            "edge_cache_settings": {
                "enabled": True,
                "value": "4d",
                "custom_values": {"200": "10m", "404": "1m"},
            }
        },
    )
    cache = updated.options.edge_cache_settings
    print(cache.value, cache.custom_values)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "strconv"

        gcore "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go"
        "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go/cdn"
    )

    func main() {
        client := gcore.NewClient()
        ctx := context.Background()
        resourceID, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("CDN_RESOURCE_ID"), 10, 64)
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }

        updated, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                EdgeCacheSettings: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsEdgeCacheSettings{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Value:   gcore.String("4d"),
                    CustomValues: map[string]string{
                        "200": "10m",
                        "404": "1m",
                    },
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
        cache := updated.Options.EdgeCacheSettings
        fmt.Println(cache.Value, cache.CustomValues)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="curl">
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH "https://api.gcore.com/cdn/resources/$CDN_RESOURCE_ID" \
      -H "Authorization: APIKey $GCORE_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "edge_cache_settings": {
            "enabled": true,
            "value": "4d",
            "custom_values": {
              "200": "10m",
              "404": "1m"
            }
          }
        }
      }'
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200. The saved option is:</p>

    ```json
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "value": "4d",
      "custom_values": {
        "200": "10m",
        "404": "1m"
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Disable caching

<p>Set `value` to `0s` to keep the CDN caching option enabled and leave responses `200`, `206`, `301`, and `302` uncached. To turn the option off instead, set `enabled` to `false` and still send `default` or `value`.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os

    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()
    resource_id = int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"])

    updated = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        resource_id,
        options={"edge_cache_settings": {"enabled": True, "value": "0s"}},
    )
    cache = updated.options.edge_cache_settings
    print(cache.enabled, cache.value)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">
    ```go

    import (

    func main() {
        client := gcore.NewClient()
        ctx := context.Background()
        resourceID, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("CDN_RESOURCE_ID"), 10, 64)
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }

        updated, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                EdgeCacheSettings: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsEdgeCacheSettings{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Value:   gcore.String("0s"),
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
        cache := updated.Options.EdgeCacheSettings
        fmt.Println(cache.Enabled, cache.Value)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="curl">
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH "https://api.gcore.com/cdn/resources/$CDN_RESOURCE_ID" \
      -H "Authorization: APIKey $GCORE_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "edge_cache_settings": {
            "enabled": true,
            "value": "0s"
          }
        }
      }'
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200. The saved option is:</p>

    ```json
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "value": "0s"
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<p>A path-specific lifetime uses the same `edge_cache_settings` object on a [CDN&nbsp;rule](/cdn/cdn-resource-options/rules-for-particular-files/create-a-rule-manually-or-from-a-template-to-configure-settings-for-particular-files).</p>

</MethodSection>
